analyzed_vuln.description: `iterateCIPRanks()` assumes every atom's `cipEntries[i]` gains at least one element during every refinement round. After ranking, it unconditionally writes `cipEntries[i][numIts + 1]` at line 1022. An isolated atom with no coordinated hydrogens contributes no neighbor/H entries, so its vector remains at the two seed elements created at lines 913-914. If ranking proceeds to the second round (`numIts == 1`), the code writes index 2 past that two-int allocation, causing the reported 4-byte heap-buffer-overflow. The vulnerable logic must resize/pad each entry through the rank slot before indexing (or otherwise handle zero-length refinement contributions).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The fuzzer's remaining bytes are parsed by `MolDataStreamToMol()` into a molecule and stereochemistry processing calls `assignAtomCIPRanks()`. The parsed graph must contain at least one atom with no incident bonds and no inserted hydrogen rank entries (the PoC produces such an entry), while the molecule as a whole still has non-unique CIP classes and gains ranks after the first refinement, causing `iterateCIPRanks()` to enter a second iteration. On that second iteration, the isolated atom's `cipEntries` is still size 2 but `numIts + 1` is 2, so the unchecked indexed write is out of bounds.
